presentingComplaint: Severe headache, neck stiffness and fever for 2 days
history: 34-year-old man on maintenance rituximab for follicular lymphoma (last infusion 5 weeks ago) presents with a 2-day history of frontal-occipital headache, photophobia, low-grade fever, nausea and generalised myalgia, preceded by a 3-day coryzal illness. Two colleagues at work had a 'summer flu'. No seizures, no limb weakness, no behavioural change, no rash. No recent travel, no mosquito or tick exposure, no head injury. Because of his immunosuppressed state he was admitted and started on broad empiric cover pending CSF results.
examination: Alert and fully oriented (GCS 15). Neck stiffness with positive Kernig sign. No focal neurological deficit, normal fundi, no papilloedema. No rash or petechiae. No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly. Chest, cardiovascular and abdominal examination unremarkable.
imaging: CT head performed before LP (immunocompromised host): no mass lesion, hydrocephalus or midline shift. MRI brain with contrast: no parenchymal signal change or temporal-lobe involvement to suggest encephalitis; meninges unremarkable.
microbiology: CSF multiplex PCR (BioFire ME panel): ENTEROVIRUS detected; HSV-1, HSV-2, VZV, CMV and bacterial targets NOT detected. CSF bacterial culture no growth at 48h. Blood cultures x2 no growth. HIV Ag/Ab negative.
finalDiagnosis: Enteroviral (aseptic) meningitis in a rituximab-immunosuppressed host
citations: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22e - Acute Meningitis / Viral (Aseptic) Meningitis
stewardship: Because he is immunocompromised and presented as a meningitis syndrome, empiric broad cover was started after CT/LP: ceftriaxone + vancomycin (community-acquired bacterial meningitis) PLUS ampicillin for Listeria cover given immunosuppression, PLUS aciclovir until HSV encephalitis excluded. CSF was lymphocytic with normal glucose, normal lactate, negative Gram stain and low procalcitonin - an aseptic picture. Once enterovirus PCR returned positive with negative bacterial cultures and HSV/VZV PCR, all antibacterials and aciclovir were discontinued and management de-escalated to supportive care (analgesia, antiemetics, fluids). This is the antimicrobial stewardship point: a broad empiric bundle appropriate for an immunocompromised host must be actively stopped once the aseptic/viral diagnosis is confirmed.
contraindications: Aciclovir needs adequate hydration and renal-adjusted dosing to avoid crystal nephropathy
Vancomycin requires level monitoring; combined nephrotoxin exposure should be minimised
Do not omit CT head before LP in an immunocompromised host, but do not let imaging delay empiric antimicrobials
edgeCases: If CSF glucose were low with neutrophilic pleocytosis and high lactate, treat as bacterial meningitis and continue antibiotics
High CSF protein with lymphocytosis and low glucose in an at-risk patient should prompt TB meningitis workup
Enteroviral meningitis in agammaglobulinaemia (or heavy B-cell depletion) can become chronic/relapsing and may need IVIG
Persistent altered mentation, seizures or temporal-lobe MRI change means encephalitis - do not stop aciclovir until HSV PCR negative
expectedMaiK: CT head then lumbar puncture with CSF cell count/differential, protein, glucose (with paired serum), Gram stain, culture and multiplex PCR; start empiric ceftriaxone + vancomycin + ampicillin + aciclovir after cultures drawn, then discontinue antimicrobials once CSF confirms aseptic/viral meningitis and cultures are negative; supportive care.
expectedNextQuestions: What is the nature and degree of immunosuppression (rituximab, steroids, HIV status, hypogammaglobulinaemia)?
Was there a viral prodrome, sick contacts or enteroviral-season exposure?
Any seizures, focal deficit or altered mentation to suggest encephalitis rather than meningitis?
Any rash, travel or mosquito/tick exposure pointing to an arboviral cause?
